title: Constructibility and dense-open vanishing of the normalization mono cokernel
statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field, $f:X	o\operatorname{Spec}k$ a separated finite-type morphism with $\dim X\le1$, and $X$ reduced [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring and $\ell$ a prime such that $R=\Lambda/(\ell)$ is finite as a set. Let $
u:X'	o X$ be finite and surjective, let $V\subseteq X$ be a dense open over which $
u$ is an isomorphism, and let $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ be open with pullback $j':U'\hookrightarrow X'$ and $
u':U'	o U$. For any monomorphism $\alpha:j_!\underline R_U	o
u_*j'_!\underline R_{U'}$ of small-etale sheaves of $\Lambda$-modules (extension by zero [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero], direct image [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]), $\operatorname{coker}\alpha$ is constructible [def-constructible-constructible] and its inverse image [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] on $V$ is zero.

source.place: Proof sketch: cokernel constructibility and vanishing over the isomorphism locus; arbitrary-mono generalization justified by finite stalks

proof.text: Prove constructibility of the constant quotient module sheaf using its cyclic module value and the constant geometric stalk formula; extend by zero with the complementary closed immersion. The new finite-pushforward quotient-constant lemma proves constructibility of the target. Apply constructible cokernel closure.

Use the comparison-object isomorphism over V. On every geometric stalk the source is finite: within U its stalk is R, outside U it is zero. Exact pullback and exact stalk functors preserve the mono α. An injection between finite equivalent sets is bijective. Geometric stalks reflect isomorphisms, so V^*α is an isomorphism. Pullback preserves cokernels and the cokernel of an epi is zero.
